results.summary: This project implements a high-density shift register using latch-based storage and an 8-phase clock. It uses four latches to store three bits per stage and eight parallel lanes to preserve throughput while relaxing timing. A Johnson counter generates the staggered pulses, and an optional LFSR mode provides observability. The design targets the IHP SG13G2 process and demonstrates a compact alternative to conventional DFF-based shift registers.

results.summary_before: This project is a Physically Unclonable Function (PUF) based on ring oscillator (RO) frequency comparisons. It uses an array of ring oscillators and compares their frequencies to generate a unique chip-specific response. The design is controlled via SPI and includes a PRNG for challenge generation. It is notable for its use of analog frequency variations to create a hardware security primitive.
results.summary: Nibble is a minimalistic 4-bit accumulator CPU with a Harvard architecture designed for TinyTapeout. It executes a simple 16-instruction ISA over a 2-cycle fetch-execute pipeline. The CPU exposes instruction inputs, program counter outputs, accumulator and flag outputs, and a 4-bit input port. It is intended to be used with external program memory such as an RP2040 or EEPROM.

results.summary_before: This is a 16-bit Data General Nova 1200 CPU implemented with a 4-bit nibble-serial datapath, capable of executing programs stored in external QSPI Flash and using PSRAM for data storage. It includes a UART for serial communication at 19,200 baud and drives diagnostic blinkenlights on the 7-segment display. The design requires the official Tiny Tapeout QSPI PMOD for Flash and PSRAM, and programs are written in Nova assembly and flashed via a provided Python script. Notable features include full programmability and interactive terminal I/O, though it relies on external hardware for memory and communication.
results.summary: This project implements a Cylon-style LED scanner using an 8-bit shift register. A direction flip-flop controls whether the lit bit moves left or right, and turn-around detection reverses the direction at the ends. On reset, the first LED is lit and the direction is cleared. The outputs drive eight LEDs directly.
